title: Microsoft says it has finished training MAI-Base-2, a 2.8 trillion-parameter AI model it claims needs far less computing power than a leading Chinese rival to reach the same results.
source_used: Microsoft, as reported by BigGo Finance
key_facts: Microsoft completed pre-training of MAI-Base-2, 2.8 trillion total parameters
Trained 38 days (Aug-Sep) on 16,000 Nvidia GB200 GPUs, about 50 trillion tokens; 18% visual data
Mixture-of-experts: about 80 billion parameters active during use
Microsoft claims 4.2x to 12.3x less compute than DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base for equal performance (internal evaluation)
Successor to MAI-Base-1 from June; unique training data up about 36%; no distillation from other models' outputs
Post-training ongoing; plans to offer weights to enterprise customers via Microsoft Foundry; availability and pricing undisclosed
quote_evidence: Microsoft announced on its official blog on the 16th that it has completed pre-training of "MAI-Base-2," a next-generation foundation model with a total of 2.8 trillion parameters.
According to Microsoft's internal evaluation results, MAI-Base-2 outperformed all major open-weight models used as benchmarks.
General availability timing and pricing have not yet been disclosed.
why_it_matters_hint: Efficiency claims, if confirmed, would lower the cost of training and running very large models.
notes: Investing.com original returned 403; read BigGo Finance relaying Microsoft's blog. BigGo says blog dated the 16th, other outlets report 15 Oct. Efficiency figures are Microsoft's own, not independently verified.
